enonce_markdown: In a word processor, which feature changes the amount of white space between the lines of text inside a paragraph?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Each formatting tool acts on one part of the page. Character tools act on letters, paragraph tools act on whole paragraphs, page tools act on the sheet.

### Solution

Line spacing is a paragraph setting: 1.0 gives single lines, 1.5 or 2.0 widen the gap between lines. Page margins change the blank border around the text, tab stops position text horizontally, and a header or footer is a repeated area at the top or bottom of every page. **Answer: C.**

enonce_markdown: A teacher types the title of a notice and wants it to appear exactly in the middle between the left and right margins. Which paragraph alignment must be applied to the title?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Alignment decides how the lines of a paragraph sit between the left and right margins: left, centre, right or justified.

### Solution

Centre alignment places each line of the paragraph equally distant from both margins, which is what a title needs. Left alignment starts every line at the left margin, right alignment ends it at the right margin, and justify stretches the spaces so that both edges are straight. **Answer: A.**

enonce_markdown: A secretary in Bamenda has typed a table with twelve columns. The table is too wide to fit on a portrait A4 page. Which change is the most suitable way to make the whole table fit without making the text unreadable?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Page layout settings (orientation, paper size, margins) change the sheet; they are used before shrinking text, which harms readability.

### Solution

Switching the page orientation from portrait to landscape gives a wider writing area (29.7 cm instead of 21 cm on A4) and keeps the text at a readable size. Reducing the font to 1 pt makes the text unreadable, changing to a smaller paper such as A5 makes the problem worse, and line spacing only changes the vertical gaps, not the width. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Reduce the font size to 1 pt
Change the page orientation to landscape
Change the paper size to A5

enonce_markdown: A student is typing a 20-page report and wants the page number to appear at the bottom of every page, without typing it on each page. What should the student do?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Text that must repeat on every page belongs in the header or footer area, which the word processor copies to all pages automatically.

### Solution

Insert the page number field in the **footer** (*Insert* > *Page Number* > *Bottom of Page*). The program numbers every page automatically and updates the numbers when pages are added or removed. Typing numbers by hand or in a text box on page 1 does not repeat them, and line numbering numbers the lines of text, not the pages. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Type the number by hand at the end of each page
Insert a text box with the number on page 1
Insert the page number field in the footer

corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Character and paragraph formatting is applied to a selection: select first, then choose the command. Page settings apply to the whole section or document.

### Solution

1. **Title:** select the title line (triple-click or drag over it). On the *Home* tab click **Center** (alignment), click **Bold** (B), then open the font size box and choose **16**.
2. **Body paragraph:** click inside the paragraph (or select it). Click **Justify** in the alignment group, then open **Line spacing** (*Home* > *Paragraph*) and choose **1.5**.
3. **Margins:** open the *Layout* tab > **Margins** > **Custom Margins**, type **2.5 cm** in the Top, Bottom, Left and Right boxes, and click **OK**.

A complete answer shows the order *select, then format* for items 1 and 2, and uses the page-layout menu (not the space bar or the Enter key) for item 3.

enonce_markdown:
Fon typed an invitation card in a word processor. To place the title in the middle he pressed the space bar about twenty times before it. At the end of every line of a paragraph he pressed the Enter key, and he aligned a list of items and their prices with several spaces. After he changed the font size, the title moved off-centre, the paragraph broke into short lines and the prices no longer lined up.

Identify the three mistakes and, for each one, give the correct method.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The word processor already has tools for layout. Using spaces and Enter to imitate them gives a layout that breaks as soon as the font, the size or the page changes.

### Solution

1. **Title centred with spaces.** Spaces have a width that depends on the font and size, so the title moves when these change. Correct method: remove the spaces and apply **Center** alignment to the title paragraph.
2. **Enter at the end of every line.** The program wraps text automatically at the right margin; each Enter creates a new paragraph, so when the size changes the lines no longer fill the width and break in the wrong places. Correct method: type the paragraph continuously and press Enter **only at the end of the paragraph**.
3. **Prices aligned with spaces.** Different characters have different widths, so spaces cannot give an exact column. Correct method: use a **tab stop** (press Tab between the item and its price, with a right or decimal tab set on the ruler) or insert a two-column table.

The common idea: the layout is controlled by alignment, wrapping and tab stops, not by blank characters.
